newsitem.title: USA: RARE Hospitality sees Q2 below views.
newsitem.headline: RARE Hospitality sees Q2 below views.

text.p: RARE Hospitality International Inc said on Monday that it expected earnings for its second quarter ending June 29 to be lower than analysts' estimates, partly as a result of increased restaurant-level costs of food and labor.

Specifically, the company said it expected earnings for the quarter to be in the range of $0.16 to $0.18 per share, or about 35 percent below the $0.25 per share to $0.27 per share estimates of analysts regularly following the company.
Meanwhile, RARE Hospitality said it expects revenues to be within the ranges of analysts' expectations.

"Early in the quarter, we began to implement menu changes in the LongHorn system that included an upgrade of product presentations and the addition of a new steak. The consumer response was stronger than expected, resulting in a significant shift in mix and an increase in food costs," said company president Richard Rivera.
"Labor costs and controllable expenses increased as well," he added.
